claims.statement: Blanching, moisture and retained sensation favor shallower dermal injury; a dry nonblanching insensate region raises concern for full-thickness injury.
claims.limitation: Regional and serial examination is necessary; no single bedside finding proves histologic depth.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: A burn may deepen after its first assessment; peripheral epithelialization does not establish recovery of a poorly perfused central region.
claims.limitation: Constructed serial observations require burn-clinician review; no fixed conversion timeline is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: A minor burn may receive local outpatient wound care and reassessment when wound, pain and follow-up needs fit local capability.
claims.limitation: Both NSW publications are from one health system. Local referral arrangements differ; consultation is not synonymous with transfer.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Burns affecting the hand or major joints warrant burn-specialist assessment when depth or function is concerning.
claims.limitation: Urgency and physical transfer depend on physiology and receiving-team assessment; no automatic operation is implied.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: A small burn can require specialist care if dressing and analgesia needs exceed the treating clinic's resources.
claims.limitation: Single independent health-system source family; no analgesic dose or pain-score threshold is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Progressive voice or breathing changes after enclosed-space smoke exposure require emergency airway-capable assessment even before measured hypoxemia.
claims.limitation: Facial soot or singed hair in isolation is not a universal mandate for intubation. Clinic action is EMS transfer; hospital airway treatment is reviewed retrospectively.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: An evolving obstructed airway takes priority over diagnostic bronchoscopy in a patient with smoke injury.
claims.limitation: No device, induction drug or preemptive-intubation threshold is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Conventional pulse saturation and arterial oxygen tension do not exclude CO poisoning; blood co-oximetry measures carboxyhemoglobin.
claims.limitation: Venous or arterial blood is acceptable. Oxygen administration and elapsed time change the measured level.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Prior loss of consciousness, persistent neurologic abnormalities or cardiac injury can justify hyperbaric consultation despite a low COHb measured after oxygen.
claims.limitation: One directly verified current clinical source. Consultation for possible HBO is keyed, not a claim of proven universal benefit or mandatory treatment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: An enclosed-space fire followed by profound lactic acidosis and circulatory collapse can support empiric hydroxocobalamin for suspected cyanide toxicity.
claims.limitation: Lactate is not specific; synthetic values are observations, not a new diagnostic threshold. No exact dose, infusion time or universal antidote trigger authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: A methemoglobin-forming cyanide antidote can further compromise oxygen carriage when CO poisoning coexists.
claims.limitation: Regulatory safety warning, not an absolute prohibition on nitrite use or proof of comparative outcome benefit. Initial JTS-only support gap was repaired by targeted official-label verification.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: After airway stabilization, bronchoscopy can directly assess and grade smoke-related lower-airway injury when an initial chest radiograph is unrevealing.
claims.limitation: One directly verified guideline; CT and radiography assess other injury patterns and are not substitutes for direct airway examination.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Epidermal erythema is excluded from the partial/full-thickness TBSA used in burn-resuscitation estimates.
claims.limitation: Fictional regional percentages are supplied in the case; no protected body diagram or age-proportion algorithm is reproduced.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: An initial burn-fluid estimate must be adjusted to serial urine output and perfusion rather than delivered unchanged despite evidence of excessive resuscitation.
claims.limitation: Guidelines use different initial formulas and urine targets. No universal starting multiplier, exact titration percentage or electrical-injury output target is keyed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: NSW guidance describes a starting estimate of 3 mL/kg per percent dermal-burn TBSA over the first day, with half allocated during the first eight hours measured from injury.
claims.limitation: One regional protocol, explicitly supplied as this fictional hospital's worksheet. Not a universal Parkland/ABA/JTS formula. Patient arithmetic is constructed; subsequent titration is a separate decision.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: A restrictive circumferential deep thermal burn with worsening distal perfusion despite adequate systemic resuscitation may require escharotomy.
claims.limitation: Reassess dressings, elevation and perfusion; skin release does not treat every deep muscle-compartment problem.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Circumferential deep chest-wall burns can restrict ventilation and require chest escharotomy when the mechanical restriction is clinically significant.
claims.limitation: Tube obstruction, pneumothorax and parenchymal disease remain alternatives; the constructed record supplies relevant checks without an exact pressure cutoff.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: A small skin wound after high-voltage injury can conceal major muscle damage with pigmenturia and kidney risk.
claims.limitation: Skin TBSA does not quantify electrical deep-tissue damage. No exact voltage or CK threshold is needed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: High-voltage muscle injury can cause a deep compartment syndrome requiring fascial decompression rather than skin eschar release.
claims.limitation: Single directly verified source. The draft includes serial compartment findings; a separate current JTS compartment guideline supports the examination. No numerical pressure cutoff is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Progressive pain on passive muscle stretch and weakness after a substantial extremity injury can indicate compartment syndrome even when arterial pulses remain present.
claims.limitation: One current government guideline. Tension alone is not a reliable exclusion test; no single symptom or numerical pressure cutoff is treated as definitive.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: A rise in both peak and plateau pressure favors reduced respiratory-system compliance, whereas an isolated peak rise can reflect increased flow resistance.
claims.limitation: Context only for the burn chest-release decision. Requires an interpretable passive measurement; no pressure target or general ventilator-management question is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Dry chemical residue should be removed before copious irrigation; routine acid-base neutralization on skin can cause further injury.
claims.limitation: Ranked research gap only; no scored dry-powder item added in this packet. Specific agents can need additional toxicology advice.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Systemic fluoride absorption can lower calcium and magnesium and disturb potassium, causing neuromuscular and cardiac toxicity.
claims.limitation: Archived ATSDR physiology cross-checked against current transfer guidance; local burn size alone does not establish systemic safety.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Systemic hypocalcemia after HF exposure is treated with intravenous calcium under ECG and electrolyte surveillance.
claims.limitation: One directly verified specific treatment source, explicitly archived. Exact dose, concentration and local/intra-arterial pathways are withheld; clinician/toxicology review required.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Extensive-burn patients unable to eat may receive early enteral nutrition after resuscitation when the gastrointestinal tract is usable.
claims.limitation: No exact-hour cutoff or full-calorie prescription authored. Older critical-care guidance and one current regional source are not two new burn trials.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Absent or quiet bowel sounds alone do not establish an enteral-feeding contraindication after perfusion recovery.
claims.limitation: Single older society guideline, weak recommendation. Obstruction, bowel ischemia and uncontrolled shock remain separate contraindications.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: New uncontrolled shock or concern for intestinal ischemia warrants pausing enteral delivery during urgent reassessment.
claims.limitation: Single older society guideline; low-certainty expert guidance. A postpyloric tube does not restore bowel perfusion. No pressor cutoff or automatic immediate PN prescription follows.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Deep burn regions commonly need removal of nonviable tissue and coverage, while viable epithelializing regions can be preserved.
claims.limitation: No fixed excision day or predetermined graft area is imposed; a burn surgeon must confirm regional depth and readiness.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Cadaveric allograft can temporarily cover an excised extensive burn when the patient's available donor skin is insufficient for immediate autografting.
claims.limitation: One independent health-system source family. Not a general graft-take question; product comparisons and mandatory timing of replacement are outside scope.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Systemic antimicrobial treatment is reserved for burn infection or another indication rather than routine prophylaxis of a clinically uninfected burn.
claims.limitation: A positive surface swab alone does not establish invasive infection. No numeric fever cutoff or empiric regimen is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: A colonized burn wound that continues to heal without clinical infection can be managed with local antimicrobial wound care and reassessment rather than automatic systemic antibiotics.
claims.limitation: Delayed healing, tissue deterioration or clinical infection changes the decision; this is not a rule to dismiss every positive culture or invasive organism.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: A postpyloric route may address persistent gastric delivery problems but is not a workaround for suspected bowel ischemia or uncontrolled shock.
claims.limitation: One older society guideline; exact aspirate thresholds and advancement protocols are not authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Constricting circumferential burn dressings can impair distal circulation; remove an external constriction and reassess neurovascular findings before attributing it to burn eschar or deep muscle compartments.
claims.limitation: One health-system source family. The exact first response is an anatomic/chronologic synthesis of dressing precautions and escharotomy indications; persistent compromise requires urgent specialist escalation, not repeated dressing trials.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Burn procedural analgesia should be assessed during the actual dressing procedure after premedication has taken effect; resting comfort alone does not establish adequate wound-care tolerance.
claims.limitation: One health-system source family. A completed observed procedure supports a local care arrangement only for comparable future care; no drug dose, onset interval or guarantee of future tolerance is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Persistent oliguria after muscle injury does not by itself justify repeated fluid escalation when systemic perfusion has recovered and fluid is accumulating; reassess renal injury, drainage and volume status and limit further unnecessary crystalloid.
claims.limitation: Direction-only decision after documented volume assessment. No urine target, exact fluid reduction, mandatory diuretic or dialysis prescription is inferred. No dynamic-test threshold is invented.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: After smoke injury and airway stabilization, bronchoscopy can inspect the lower airway and remove retained carbonaceous material or casts contributing to airway obstruction.
claims.limitation: Single current guideline. Ventilator mechanics and tube/pleural checks localize the constructed problem; bronchoscopy is not a substitute for initial airway stabilization.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: During valid passive ventilator measurements, a rising peak pressure with unchanged plateau pressure favors increased flow resistance rather than a new compliance problem.
claims.limitation: Single government guideline; applied only to the burn-specific lower-airway complication here. Values are paired fictional measurements, not clinical pressure targets. The original chest-release-context atom remains unchanged.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Assessment of new ventilatory difficulty includes tube position and patency and pleural causes before attributing the problem to material beyond the endotracheal tube.
claims.limitation: Government-guideline clinical synthesis. A passing catheter or one pleural observation alone does not exclude every tube or pleural problem; the full acquired pattern determines the preferred procedure.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: Before burn graft coverage, residual nonviable eschar is removed to prepare a viable bleeding recipient bed; temporary coverage does not make retained dead tissue an adequate recipient bed.
claims.limitation: One health-system source family. No exact excision depth, schedule or product ranking is taught. The full constructed operative plan requires burn-surgeon review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

claims.statement: After perfusion is controlled, persistent large gastric aspirates despite prokinetic treatment can support postpyloric enteral feeding if bowel ischemia or obstruction is not suspected.
claims.limitation: Single older society guideline; weak/low-certainty recommendation. Fictional aspirate volumes are observations, not a newly invented threshold. Exact tube-placement technique and feeding advancement remain outside scope.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thermal, smoke, electrical or chemical injury; hospital decisions are reviewed from clinic.

discrepanciesAndWithheldTeachingPoints.reason: JTS and NSW use different starting protocols. One stated regional worksheet is supplied; no universal multiplier or ABA recommendation inferred.
NSW adult decrease-output units appear inconsistent in the published text and differ from JTS targets/increments. No disputed units or exact percentage changes taught.
JTS and regulator descriptions differ in exact infusion timing and lactate context. No dose, infusion time or universal diagnostic threshold authored.
JTS/NSW time windows and operational settings differ. Regional coverage is scored without a mandatory operation day.
ATSDR is archived; local concentrations differ across guidance. Exact dose, concentration, local/intra-arterial ranking and discharge duration withheld.

Dry-powder decontamination, electrical cardiac-disposition details, topical-product superiority, scar/contracture procedure ranking and nutrition targets need further bounded evidence/scenario work. No fake keyed or unkeyed item created.
